results.title: Private LLM hosting vs Lambda Labs for EU companies | GPUwerk
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
I run GPUwerk, which rents DGX Sparks, so weigh everything below with that in mind. Of all the providers on these pages, Lambda is the closest to GPUwerk in shape: GPU machines rented by running time and billed by the minute, with no per-token pricing. Lambda offers many NVIDIA GPU types, from a single A10 to 8-GPU B200 machines, in 14 regions including one in Germany. GPUwerk offers one machine, a DGX Spark with 128 GB of unified memory, in Hradec Králové, at one rate. Lambda wins on GPU range and raw speed; a Spark wins on memory per dollar for a single machine.

...

| | Lambda Labs | Dedicated DGX Spark (GPUwerk) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | A US-headquartered GPU cloud: on-demand virtual machines across NVIDIA GPU types, plus clusters and longer-term reservations. | A GPU cloud provider too, but with one hardware option: a dedicated DGX Spark, rented by the hour. (advantage) |
| Region | 14 regions in Lambda's docs, among them europe-central-1 (Germany), several US regions, Japan, India and Israel. Not every instance type is available in every region. | Own Sparks in Hradec Králové, Czechia; partner Sparks in other EEA countries, the US and Hong Kong. The console offers one Europe (EEA) location. |
| Hardware choice | From a single A10, GH200 or H100 PCIe up to 8-GPU A100, H100 and B200 machines. | One machine: the DGX Spark, 128GB unified memory, with an optional two-node cluster for larger workloads. |
| Who can see your data | Governed by whichever terms and data processing addendum Lambda offers for your account and region; check Lambda's own legal pages for the current text. | No other customer, and GPUwerk only under the DPA. GPUwerk's DPA states GPUwerk "hosts the machine but does not access, read, copy, index, or analyse the content of the controller's instance." (advantage) |
| Model choice | Whatever you deploy, unrestricted by the provider. Larger multi-GPU instances can run bigger models or serve higher concurrency than a single Spark. | Whatever you deploy too, but bounded by 128GB unified memory: gpt-oss-120b, Llama 3.3 70B, Qwen3-Coder 30B, DeepSeek, and similar fit; models that need substantially more memory or multi-node sharding don't, without moving to the two-node cluster. |
| Speed and concurrency | Depends entirely on the GPU type and count you rent; Lambda publishes instance specs but the achievable tok/s for a given model is yours to benchmark. | A single Spark, single-stream: gpt-oss-120b decodes at 33.5 tok/s and reaches 862.8 tok/s aggregate at 256 concurrent requests (Dendro Logic's concurrency benchmark, run on their own Spark). Raw logs and methodology on GPUwerk's benchmarks page. (advantage) |
| Pricing model | Priced per GPU-hour, billed in one-minute increments. On lambda.ai/pricing (checked 9 November 2026), in effect from 16 November 2026: A10 $1.29, GH200 $2.59, H100 PCIe $3.79, H100 SXM (8x) $4.59 and B200 (8x) $7.69 per GPU-hour. | Per hour, billed per minute: $0.79/hour on-demand, $0.59/hour while stopped and held for you. One rate regardless of workload, per pricing. (advantage) |
| Worked cost example | See the full arithmetic below the table. | |
| Contracts and DPA | Governed by Lambda's own customer agreement and data processing terms; check Lambda's current legal pages for the specifics that apply to your account. | A standard GDPR Article 28 DPA published free at /legal/dpa, no negotiation required. Sub-processor list at /legal/sub-processors states none are engaged for instance workloads. (advantage) |
| What you operate yourself | Everything on the instance: OS, model server, monitoring, backups. Lambda manages the physical hardware and network underneath. | The same: root access, from the browser terminal or over SSH with your own key, to your own container, the model server, any RAG or agent layer, monitoring, and backups. GPUwerk keeps no copy of /workspace, not even for a failed drive, so that responsibility is entirely yours. |

...

Lambda Labs. The cheapest single-GPU instance that holds gpt-oss-120b is an 80 GB H100 PCIe at $3.79/hour, or a GH200 at $2.59/hour, per the rates Lambda's pricing page lists from 16 November 2026. Both are much faster per request than a Spark, so measure your model's tokens per second on the one you would use and work out the hours for 500 million tokens.

...

Lambda claims checked on 9 November 2026 against lambda.ai/pricing (GPU-hour prices), Lambda's On-Demand Cloud docs (regions, virtual machines) and billing docs (one-minute increments). Prices change; check the instance you would run. Spark throughput figures come from Dendro Logic's concurrency benchmark, detailed on GPUwerk's benchmarks page.

results.title: Private LLM hosting vs CoreWeave for EU companies | GPUwerk
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
I run GPUwerk, which rents DGX Sparks, so weigh everything below with that in mind.

| | CoreWeave | Dedicated DGX Spark (GPUwerk) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it's built for | Large-scale training and inference clusters: many GPUs, high-speed interconnect, Kubernetes-native orchestration, sized for AI labs and enterprise workloads. | One dedicated machine for one team's inference workload. Not built to scale to multi-node training; that's not the product. (advantage) |
| GPU hardware | A range of current-generation NVIDIA data-center GPUs at cluster scale; specific availability and generation mix change over time; check CoreWeave's own capacity pages. | NVIDIA DGX Spark: Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified memory, one unit per instance. (advantage) |
| Commitment and minimums | On-demand rates are published for most GPU types, and committed usage is discounted by up to 60%. The newest systems are sold through sales. | No minimum term. $0.79/hour on-demand, billed per minute, cancel any time. (advantage) |
| Where data is processed | Whichever CoreWeave data center region you provision in; region selection and current EU footprint should be confirmed on CoreWeave's own site. | Own Sparks in Hradec Králové, Czechia; partner Sparks in other EEA countries, the US and Hong Kong. The console offers one Europe (EEA) location. |
| Who can see your data | Governed by CoreWeave's own customer agreement and data processing terms; review those directly for the specifics of access and subprocessors. | No other customer, and GPUwerk only under the DPA. GPUwerk's DPA states GPUwerk hosts the machine but does not access, read, copy, index, or analyse the content of the controller's instance. (advantage) |
| Pricing model | Per instance-hour, mostly 8-GPU machines. On-demand examples on coreweave.com/pricing (North America, checked 9 November 2026): HGX H100 (8 GPUs) $49.24/hour, HGX B200 (8 GPUs) $68.80/hour, L40S (8 GPUs) $18.00/hour. | One flat rate regardless of workload: $0.79/hour on-demand, $0.59/hour while stopped and held for you, billed per minute. Per pricing. (advantage) |
| Operational model | Managed Kubernetes-native platform with CoreWeave-specific tooling (CKS, Slurm on Kubernetes, storage and networking products) layered on top of raw compute. | Root access, from the browser terminal or over SSH with your own key, to a container on the Spark. No managed orchestration layer; you run vLLM, LiteLLM, or whatever stack you choose yourself. |

...

Most of CoreWeave's published on-demand machines are 8-GPU instances (the exception is a single-GPU GH200 at $6.50/hour); an 8-GPU L40S instance at $18.00/hour costs about $13,140 for the same 730 hours, and an 8-GPU H100 instance about $35,945. That is a different scale of machine, with far more compute, and committed use cuts it by up to 60%. If your workload needs several GPUs with fast interconnect, or you are training rather than serving, CoreWeave can be much cheaper per unit of work. If you need one machine for inference and no contract, the Spark's $576.70 a month or $0.79/hour is the simpler number to plan around.

...

For one machine, yes, because they are different sizes of purchase. CoreWeave's on-demand prices are for multi-GPU instances, for example $49.24/hour for an 8-GPU HGX H100 machine in North America on its pricing page (checked 9 November 2026), with up to 60% off for committed usage. A GPUwerk Spark is $0.79/hour with no minimum term: one machine, hourly, no contract. Per unit of compute at scale, CoreWeave can come out cheaper.

...

CoreWeave prices checked on 9 November 2026 against coreweave.com/pricing (on-demand instance prices, committed-use discount). CoreWeave's region documentation needs an access code, so the EU footprint on this page is not verified; confirm it with CoreWeave. GPUwerk's figures ($0.79/hour, $0.59/hour, $576.70/month) come from GPUwerk's published pricing.

results.title: Private LLM hosting vs Hetzner GPU servers | GPUwerk

I run GPUwerk, which rents DGX Sparks, so weigh everything below with that in mind. Hetzner, the German hosting company, rents dedicated GPU servers (its GEX line) in Germany and Finland, with no minimum contract. Its largest card is an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q with 96 GB of GDDR7, and the GEX430 puts four of them in one server. A DGX Spark is one machine with 128 GB of unified memory, rented by the minute. The choice is about memory layout, billing and how much server you want to run yourself, not price alone.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

## The disclosure and our analysis

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

This is not the first increase. The Motley Fool reports that in early May, Nebius's pricing page showed H100 at $2.95 per hour and B300 at $6.10. [2] Our own catalog recorded H100 at $3.85 on September 18 and B300 at $7.85 on September 24.

...

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.

results.title: Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October By Investing.com
highlights:
Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

results.title: Nebius Said to Raise Prices for its On-demand Compute Resources Starting October | MemoryMarket - memory prices, market analysis, industry news, research report
results.author: By: M
highlights: According to media reports, Nebius will raise prices for some of its on-demand computing resources starting October 1, marking the company's second round of price increases since May. Under the new pricing plan, the price of H100 will rise from $3.85 per GPU hour to $4.50, an increase of about 17%; H200 will rise 20% from $4.50 to $5.40; B200 will rise nearly 19% from $7.15 to $8.50; and B300 will rise about 21% from $7.85 per GPU hour to $9.50. The changes also extend to CPU-only compute. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates will rise 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour from $0.012, while Genoa memory will increase about 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. The ultimate impact on customers' bills will therefore depend on their configurations and usage.

results.title: Nebius to Raise GPU Cloud Pricing Across H100, H200
results.author: MarketCatalyst Desk
highlights:
# Nebius to Raise GPU Cloud Pricing Across H100, H200, B200 and B300 Starting Oct. 1

Nebius will raise on-demand GPU cloud pricing across H100, H200, B200 and B300 starting October 1, as it scales capacity and secures financing tied to deployed GPUs.

Published Sep 17, 2026 · 4:44 PM ET · 4 min read

...

Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) is planning to raise prices on several of its on-demand GPU, CPU, and memory services starting October 1, according to a customer pricing notice reviewed by MarketCatalyst. The adjustments touch the company's most sought-after compute tiers — NVIDIA's H100, H200, B200, and B300 chips — and follow a strong second quarter shaped by rising AI Cloud demand.

...

## What's Changing

The notice lists new per-GPU-hour rates across four NVIDIA chip families, plus adjustments to underlying CPU and memory pricing:

| Hardware | New Rate | Previous Rate | Region(s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H100 | $4.50 / GPU-hr | $3.85 / GPU-hr | eu-north1 |
| NVIDIA H200 | $5.40 / GPU-hr | $4.50 / GPU-hr | Listed European & U.S. regions |
| NVIDIA B200 | $8.50 / GPU-hr | $7.15 / GPU-hr | us-central1, me-west1 |
| NVIDIA B300 | $9.50 / GPU-hr | $7.85 / GPU-hr | uk-south1, eu-west2, us-north1 |

The increases range from roughly 15% for the H100 and H200 to about 21% for the B300, which sees the largest adjustment of the four. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU and memory rates are also moving slightly higher as part of the same notice, while Intel Ice Lake CPU pricing remains unchanged.

The bottom line

Every chip seeing a price increase is a current-generation or near-current NVIDIA accelerator used for AI training and inference, rather than older, lower-demand hardware. This pattern is consistent with a company adjusting prices where capacity is tightest, rather than where it may be trying to move idle inventory.

...

The rate changes are set to take effect October 1 across the regions listed above. Customers with existing reserved or contracted capacity commitments are typically governed by separate contract terms rather than these on-demand list prices, though the notice offers a useful signal on the broader direction of AI compute costs as capacity remains tight across the industry.

...

### When do Nebius's new GPU prices take effect?

According to a customer pricing notice, the new rates for H100, H200, B200, and B300 GPUs, along with AMD EPYC Genoa CPU and memory pricing, are set to take effect October 1.

### How much are Nebius's GPU prices increasing?

H100 pricing in eu-north1 is set to rise to $4.50 per GPU-hour from $3.85. H200 pricing is set to rise to $5.40 per GPU-hour from $4.50 across listed European and U.S. regions. B200 pricing in us-central1 and me-west1 is set to rise to $8.50 from $7.15 per GPU-hour. B300 pricing in uk-south1, eu-west2, and us-north1 is set to rise to $9.50 from $7.85 per GPU-hour.
